No blocking introduced code defect was found; the repository-required upgrade qualification remains outstanding. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `9f9de44a54e678d62f291712db0aa049c2ebd94f` ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A focused repair with meaningful regression coverage and no identified blocking code defect, pending upgrade qualification. | | **Proof confidence** | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Not applicable: The ordinary external-contributor proof gate does not apply to this maintainer-authored PR. Its reported candidate tests exercise call-drain rollback, monitor replacement, and model-request recovery; the separate repository upgrade qualification remains required. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Not applicable | Not applicable: The ordinary external-contributor proof gate does not apply to this maintainer-authored PR. Its reported candidate tests exercise call-drain rollback, monitor replacement, and model-request recovery; the separate repository upgrade qualification remains required. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 9 items | Introduced change ownership: Reviewed the pinned merge-base-to-head delta. The supplied verified test merge has the pinned base followed by the exact PR head as parents; unrelated endpoint drift was excluded.
Reversible pre-stop wait: The added call-only drain precedes previousStopStarted, rechecks current ownership before stopping anything, and routes timeout through the existing reversible rollback. The cleanup helper prevents an expired observation from quiescing later instances after rollback.
Channel monitor custody: The single channel startup site retains a custody consumer until the monitor settles. Existing channel account capability revocation, stop ownership, and post-stop consumer drainage remain in place; no public plugin API or persisted setting is added. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together The Gateway’s plugin lifecycle receives reload requests and coordinates running calls, channel monitors, services, and model preparation. It publishes a replacement generation only after the previous owners safely release their resources. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Plugin reload request] --> B[Reserve replacement and pause admission] B --> C[Wait for active calls] C -->|Calls settle| D[Stop channels and services] D --> E[Publish replacement generation] C -->|Deadline expires| F[Resume previous generation] F --> G[Restore model preparation and readiness] ``` ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Configured-channel startup and shutdown after an upgrade remain unqualified for the changed monitor lifetime; candidate tests do not establish survival through the published updater and managed-service restart. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Attach sanitized published-updater-to-candidate evidence showing existing configured channels and their settings survive managed-service restart and return to readiness.

### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Production versus regression growth** | Production net +101 lines; tests and test support net +214 lines | Production growth is justified by the shared bounded-drain logic and monitor custody; most added coverage protects rollback and resource settlement. | ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Qualify configured-channel upgrades (recommended)** Attach published-updater-to-candidate evidence showing existing channel configuration, managed-service startup, and readiness survive the changed monitor lifetime. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep replacement atomic and reversible until calls settle, preserving existing configured channels across both hot replacement and validated upgrades. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes, from source: an ordinary call that outlives drainage reaches service shutdown first on fetched main and can prevent safe recovery. The PR supplies a concrete incident and focused failing-before regressions; this review did not execute them. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes. Moving call settlement before irreversible shutdown uses the existing rollback owner and preserves the single-generation publication contract without new configuration. Existing channel account capability revocation, stop ownership, and post-stop consumer drainage remain in place; no public plugin API or persisted setting is added. ([`src/gateway/server-channel-startup.ts:23`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/9f9de44a54e678d62f291712db0aa049c2ebd94f/src/gateway/server-channel-startup.ts#L23), [9f9de44a54e6](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/9f9de44a54e678d62f291712db0aa049c2ebd94f)) - **Failure publication and regression coverage:** Model-runtime rollback now runs after uncommitted failures even when plugin recovery fails. The merged https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151738 protects retained work, while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/151588 releases idle publication custody; neither supplies this pre-stop ordinary-call wait. No merged replacement for this PR was established. The captured current body reports candidate tests, but no such upgrade cell. The configured-channel upgrade evidence in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/150953 targets a different candidate.
